doc.title: Eric Alexander interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010

chapter: Coming up: Indiana and William Paterson
title: Hearing the practice rooms at Indiana University
summary: At Indiana he heard students doing things he could not imagine, felt a competitive impulse, and discovered records he had never heard.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: I didn’t really have a specific moment, but what I can tell you is I’m wearing this shirt today interestingly enough. I went to Indiana University right out of high school. And I wasn’t even sure I wanted to play music but I was involved in the jazz program there as part of an overall liberal arts degree. Within the first week of arriving there, I heard people in the practice rooms at the music school doing things I couldn’t believe. You know I hadn’t heard people do that before. And my first thought was oh my God, I’ll never be able to do that. But that thought was shortly followed by I’m going to figure that out and do it better than them. You know, sort of like a competitive impulse. And then of course I met other students there who had record collections. They had all these things that I had never heard. So they’re playing this music that, it’s really like I’d been waiting my whole life to hear this music and never had a chance to really hear it. So when suddenly you’re given these kinds of experiences or you have these kinds of experiences, I mean if you’re ready for it it’s kind of like a dormant volcano inside you that just really takes you over.
